purpose: Human assessment of COOLING ARCHITECTURE from aerial imagery, used as a SCOPE GATE on top of refusal_rank.py's measured physics ranking. PLAN section 8d's scope statement depends on this: it only holds where cooling equipment draws air within a few metres of grade, because that is what makes FortyGuard's 2 m measurement plane the plane the equipment breathes.
why_a_human_gate: Classifying rooftop vs grade equipment is a judgement from imagery, not a computation. It is recorded here, per candidate, with the evidence, so it can be challenged. It is NOT inferred from any automated metric.
resolution_caveat: ESRI World Imagery and USGS National Map are ~0.3-0.5 m. At that scale we see OBJECTS, not nameplates. We cannot certify whether a unit is a chiller, a condenser, an air handler or a fan, and we cannot measure heights. The grade-vs-roof distinction is what is claimed, nothing finer.
two_source_rule: No verdict is recorded from a single source. ESRI and USGS have different capture seasons, so agreement between them is meaningful.

assessed_2026_08_18.name: Amazon Web Services IAD116 -> IAD117

A LONG ROW OF LARGE RECTANGULAR UNITS SITS AT GRADE IN THE GAP BETWEEN THE TWO HALLS, running most of the gap length, with distinct shadows and clearly outside the roof outlines. assessed_2026_08_18.consequence: Satisfies PLAN section 8d, and the grade-level equipment lies IN THE GAP -- exactly where the modelled plume path runs. SELECTED.

multisite_note_2026_08_19: TWO OF THREE new candidate sites FAILED this gate, and neither failure was detectable from OSM tags, wind climatology, weather-record quality or the measured refusal ranking. Santa Clara had the strongest numbers of all three and is out of scope; Phoenix's pair is not built. The gate prevented ~8,440 credits being spent on fields for sites the physics cannot honestly model.
santaclara_metro_level_2026_08_19: TWO OF TWO screened pairs are ROOFTOP, and the pattern has a plausible cause rather than being bad luck: Santa Clara is a dense, expensive, largely RETROFIT market -- multi-storey buildings on small parcels, so plant goes on the roof. Ashburn is greenfield: sprawling single-storey halls with room for grade-level equipment yards. If that reading is right, PLAN section 8d's scope premise -- that FortyGuard's 2 m plane is the plane the equipment breathes -- fits GREENFIELD campuses and not dense retrofit markets, which is a genuine and quotable limit on where this agent applies. TREATED AS A STRONG INDICATION, NOT PROOF: five further annotated frames (ranks 3-7) remain unscreened, and rank 7 has usable_exposure 0.0000 so it is worthless anyway. No FortyGuard call was bought for this metro.
dulles_why_it_matters_2026_08_19: This site was added on the user's request for recognisable operators, but chosen on MEASURED grounds rather than for the logo. The cluster holds 24 tagged data centres of 31 buildings (77 %, matching Ashburn's 75 % and far above Chicago's 4 % or Phoenix's 7 %), operated by Amazon Web Services (9), Google (3), Microsoft (2), Digital Realty (2) and CyrusOne (1) -- including a 198,921 m2 Google Data Center and a 136,947 m2 Microsoft Data Center. Decisively, station KIAD is 6.7 km away (closer than the 8.9 km to our own committed Ashburn site) and its 43,763-hour record ALREADY EXISTS, so this metro required no ASOS fetch, no new conformal calibration and carried no coverage-floor risk. It shares Ashburn's climate and station on purpose: that isolates GEOMETRY and OPERATOR from weather, making it a genuinely different SITE rather than a different climate.
dulles_status_2026_08_19: UNRESOLVED, and honestly so. Rank 1 (Amazon IAD121 -> IAD122) is the CLEAREST grade-cooled pair screened across five metros -- clean roofs, chiller rows at grade on the facades that face each other -- but its 54.7 m facade-to-facade gap FAILS the corrected 60 m geometric floor, and solver.assert_intake_clear() refused to write it: 4 % of the intake averaging disc would sit on condenser source cells, i.e. the disc would average the discharge it is meant to measure. Rank 2 is rejected above. The most promising untested candidate is Amazon IAD81 -> Amazon IAD62 at a 138 m gap, which clears the floor comfortably; ranks 3 (58 m) and several others are below it. NO FortyGuard call has been bought for dulles.
